{{Quote|You will find that bold harlot that calls herself a sister, Aelta. Once you have done so, kill her.... painfully.|Gethzerion to her assassin|<ref name="SWG" />}}
'''Aelta''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Witch/Legends|witch]] who lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. She was adopted by [[Augwynne Djo]], leader of the [[Singing Mountain Clan]], following the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of two of Djo's biological daughters, [[Allaya Djo|Allaya]] and [[Kara'Teel]], and the loss of yet two other daughters, [[Barukka]] and [[Gethzerion]], to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] sect. When Gethzerion learned that her mother had adopted Aelta into her [[Djo family|family]] and turned her into a [[Sister (Witches of Dathomir)|Sister]] of the Singing Mountain Clan, she became enraged, and ordered an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] of hers to eliminate the [[Witches of Dathomir|Dathomiri Witch]].

==Biography==
===Adoption by Augwynne Djo===
{{Quote|You will be ending the short life of Sister Aelta, one of the Singing Mountain Sisters. Ever since Augwynne, Clan Mother of the Singers, has lost both of her daughters she has ''adopted'' two more. You will show that old crone that I will not accept this.|Gethzerion to her assassin|<ref name="SWG" />}}
A [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Witch/Legends|witch]] by the name of Aelta lived on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Elsewhere on Dathomir, [[Augwynne Djo]], leader of the [[Singing Mountain Clan]] of [[Witches of Dathomir|Dathomiri Witches]], mothered three daughters, including [[Gethzerion]], [[Barukka]], [[Kara'Teel]], and [[Allaya Djo|Allaya]]. However, Gethzerion and Barukka betrayed the Singing Mountain Clan, turned to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], and became [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]]. Djo's other two daughters ended up [[Death/Legends|dying]]<ref name="CTD">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref> by the time following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="SWG" /> Allaya ended up getting killed in battle, while Djo's youngest child, Kara'Teel, died while trying to protect her mother.<ref name="CTD" /> Following the deaths of these two children, Augwynne Djo decided to adopt Aelta as a new daughter. Meanwhile, Gethzerion sought refuge in Dathomir's [[Nightsister Stronghold]].<ref name="SWG" />
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars Galaxies}}
===Gethzerion's Dagger===
{{Quote|You have proven yourself adequate to my uses. I hereby name you my Dagger... and from now on you will be my personal assassin. I now need you to target your first victim.|Gethzerion to her assassin|<ref name="SWG" />}}
When Gethzerion learned that her mother had adopted Aelta into her [[Djo family|family]] and turned her into a [[Sister (Witches of Dathomir)|Sister]] of the Singing Mountain Clan, she became enraged, and ordered an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] of hers to eliminate the adopted daughter, who also held the title of [[Arch Witch]]. Gethzerion's personal assassin was a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] turned [[Slavery/Legends|slave]]. After having proved themselves to the Nightsisters sect, Gethzerion released her assassin from slavery and assigned the individual the title of [[Dagger (Nightsisters)|Dagger]]. After one of Gethzerion's [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] returned with Sister Aelta's location, the Dagger set forth to eliminate her in the wilds of Dathomir. When Aelta saw Gethzerion's assassin approach her, she was surprised, as the individual did not appear like a Nightsister. Nevertheless, Aelta recognized that the individual was sent by Gethzerion, and prepared to defend herself. Although Aelta put up a fight using her [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee]] combat skills, she was ultimately killed by the assassin. This was a source of much delight to Gethzerion, who reveled in her suffering. Gethzerion hoped that Aelta's demise would serve as a warning to the Singing Mountain Clan, that Augwynne Djo should never attempt to replace her daughters again.<ref name="SWG" />

===Aelta's Legacy===
{{Quote|My left breast is warmed at the thought of the pain she felt as she died. Any of those foolish Singing sisters will do well to heed this warning : Augwynne's daughters are dead, and they will not be ''replaced''!|Gethzerion, after Aelta's assassination|<ref name="SWG" />}}
However, the death of Aelta did not yet spell the end for Augwynne Djo's family. After Aelta's demise, Gethzerion learned that Djo had adopted yet another daughter, a former friend of Gethzerion's by the name of [[Chastina]]. To add insult to injury, Djo had even given Chastina a [[Necklace/Legends|necklace]] that Gethzerion believed belonged to her. Enraged by this perceived slight, Gethzerion ordered her Dagger to rip Chastina's [[Heart/Legends|heart]] out and retrieve her necklace. In the end, Chastina met a similar fate as Aelta, thus snuffing out Augwynne Djo's adopted family.<ref name="SWG" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You were sent by Gethzerion? But you're not a Nightsister... oh well... you will still die.|Aelta to Gethzerion's assassin|<ref name="SWG" />}}
Aelta had blue skin, black [[Hair/Legends|hair]], and blue [[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. Referred to as a "harlot" by Gethzerion, Aelta was a capable fighter skilled in melee combat. She put these skills to the test against Gethzerion's assassin, however it was not enough to save her from an untimely demise.<ref name="SWG" />

==Equipment==
As she was skilled in melee combat, Aelta possessed a number of bladed weapons, including a basic [[Sword/Legends|sword]] and a [[Katana (sword)|curved sword]] intended for single [[Limb/Legends|handed]] use. She also possessed a [[power hammer]] and a two handed curved sword. During her final moments alive, Aelta wore a gray [[Singing Mountain Clan mask]] with violet details, and a blue [[Shirt|Dawn Wrap]] with a black corset piece, red collar, and violet highlights. Additional [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] included a light pink Shredder Skirt with a [[Silver/Legends|silver]] colored medallion piece, and blue colored [[Boot/Legends|boots]]. She was also equipped with a large magenta colored [[Backpack/Legends|backpack]].<ref name="SWG" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I will not kill people for a living! No!<br />That may well be the least wise thing you have ever done. Perhaps you believed this was a request? Or perhaps you think yourself on an equal level as myself that you may speak so openly? Not smart....|Gethzerion's response to players who refused to kill Aelta|<ref name="SWG" />}}
Sister Aelta was a non-player character in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], a [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> She was included in the third [[W:c:swg:Quest|quest]] given by [[W:c:swg:Gethzerion|Gethzerion]], an NPC located at the [[W:c:swg:Nightsister Stronghold|Nightsister Stronghold]] on the [[W:c:swg:Planet|planet]] [[W:c:swg:Dathomir|Dathomir]]. In the quest, players were instructed by Gethzerion to approach Aelta and kill her. Although the player could refuse to kill Aelta, or avoid partaking in the [[W:c:swg:Nightsisters|Nightsister]] quests altogether, this article assumes 100% game completion.<ref name="SWG" /> Aelta was removed from the [[W:c:swg:Star Wars Galaxies|game]] when the [[W:c:swg:Witches of Dathomir|Witches of Dathomir]] [[W:c:swg:Witches of Dathomir Theme Park|theme park]] was revamped as part of [[W:c:swg:Game Update 18.2|Game Update 18.2]] on [[November 4]], [[2010]],<ref name="GU18">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66962&resource=publish#gu182|text=Witches of Dathomir Prologue - Game Update 18.2}}</ref> and [[W:c:swg:Game Update 19|Game Update 19]] on [[December 14]], 2010.<ref name="GU19">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66962&resource=publish#gu190|text=The Witches of Dathomir - Game Update 19}}</ref>
